  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Patient notes and medical history readable straight off a lost or stolen tablet",
      "scenario": "The design caches notes and medical history in a local SQLite file. Anyone who takes a tablet home, steals one, or connects it to a laptop can copy the database file and read every cached patient's clinical history offline, with no server involved and no way for the hospital to revoke access. No encryption of the local store is specified.",
      "component": "Local SQLite database on tablet",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Nurses use a tablet app that caches patient notes and medical history offline in a local SQLite database so they can work without signal." }

      "plainLanguage": "If someone walks off with a tablet, they can read all the patient notes stored on it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Encrypt the offline patient cache with a key tied to user unlock",
        "given": "a tablet holding cached patient notes and medical history",
        "when": "the device is powered off, locked, or the SQLite file is copied off the device",
        "then": "the cached data is unreadable without a key released only after successful user authentication on the device"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Next shift's nurse sees the previous nurse's cached patients on the shared tablet",
      "scenario": "Tablets are passed between shifts but the cache is per-device, not per-user. A nurse on the next shift (or a non-clinical staff member who picks up the tablet) opens the app and reads notes for patients she has no care relationship with, because the data was downloaded under the previous nurse's authorisation and is still present locally.",
      "component": "Shift handover on shared tablet",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Devices are shared between shifts." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200", "CWE-863"],
      "plainLanguage": "Data downloaded by one nurse stays on the shared tablet and the next person to use it can read it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Scope and clear the offline cache per user at shift handover",
        "given": "a tablet shared between shifts",
        "when": "a user signs out, the shift changes, or a different user signs in",
        "then": "the previous user's cached notes are purged or cryptographically inaccessible before the new user can browse data"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Offline mode lets a stale or revoked login keep working indefinitely",
      "scenario": "Because the app is built to work 'without signal', it must authenticate the user locally and cannot check the server. An attacker with the shared tablet, or a nurse whose account was disabled after leaving, keeps using the cached session or locally stored credential to read and write patient notes; revocation never reaches the device.",
      "component": "Nurse tablet app offline authentication",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "so they can work without signal" },
        { "quote": "Devices are shared between shifts." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613", "CWE-287"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone whose access was taken away could still use the tablet offline because it cannot check with the server.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound offline access with a short local session lifetime and forced re-check",
        "given": "a tablet operating without network connectivity",
        "when": "the offline grace period expires or the device regains connectivity",
        "then": "the app re-validates the user and account status with the server and blocks access to cached notes if the session or account is no longer valid"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Server accepts queued offline edits without re-checking who may write to that patient",
      "scenario": "Offline edits are held in the local SQLite database and pushed when signal returns. A user with device access (or who modifies the SQLite file directly) can insert or alter queued records for patients and clinicians they are not authorised for; if the sync endpoint trusts the client-supplied author, patient id and timestamps, falsified clinical notes land in the record.",
      "component": "Sync API / sync client",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Offline sync of patient notes" },
        { "quote": "caches patient notes and medical history offline in a local SQLite database" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602", "CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "Edits made on the tablet could be faked or changed before they upload, and the server might just believe them.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Re-authorise every synced change server-side",
        "given": "a batch of offline edits arriving at the sync API",
        "when": "the server processes each change",
        "then": "it derives the author from the authenticated session, ignores client-supplied identity, and rejects changes for patients the user is not authorised to modify"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Clinical notes written on a shared tablet cannot be attributed to a person",
      "scenario": "With devices shared between shifts and edits created offline, a note may reach the record without a reliable author or trustworthy time of writing. In a clinical dispute or safeguarding investigation nobody can prove which nurse wrote or changed a note, and a nurse can plausibly deny an entry made under her session.",
      "component": "Offline edit queue and record audit trail",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Devices are shared between shifts." },
        { "quote": "Offline sync of patient notes" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778", "CWE-346"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because several nurses use the same tablet, you cannot tell who actually wrote a patient note.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind each offline note to an authenticated author and server-verified time",
        "given": "a note created while the tablet is offline",
        "when": "the note is stored locally and later synced",
        "then": "it carries the authenticated user id captured at creation plus device id and client time, and the server records its own receipt time and rejects entries with no authenticated author"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Conflicting offline edits silently overwrite clinical history",
      "scenario": "Two nurses on different tablets, or the same tablet across shifts, edit the same patient note while offline. A naive last-write-wins sync discards the other entry, so medication or allergy information a clinician recorded disappears from the record and care decisions are made on wrong history.",
      "component": "Sync conflict resolution",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Offline sync of patient notes" },
        { "quote": "caches patient notes and medical history offline" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-362"],
      "plainLanguage": "Two people editing the same note offline could wipe out each other's changes without anyone noticing.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Make note sync append-only with explicit conflict handling",
        "given": "two offline edits to the same patient note",
        "when": "both are synced to the server",
        "then": "neither entry is silently discarded: both versions are retained and surfaced for clinician resolution"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Cached medical history is kept on the device far longer and wider than needed",
      "scenario": "Nothing limits what is cached or for how long, so tablets accumulate notes and full medical history for patients a nurse no longer treats, including patients discharged weeks earlier. Each shared device becomes a standing copy of a large slice of the health record, multiplying the damage from any single lost or compromised tablet.",
      "component": "Local SQLite database on tablet",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "caches patient notes and medical history offline in a local SQLite database" },
        { "quote": "Devices are shared between shifts." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212", "CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "The tablet hoards patient records it no longer needs, so losing one leaks far more than it has to.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit and expire the offline cache",
        "given": "a tablet caching patient data for offline use",
        "when": "a patient leaves the nurse's current caseload or the cached record passes its retention window",
        "then": "that record is deleted from the local database automatically, without needing a manual action"
      }
    }
  ]
